personalizedFeedback.title: LOWER THIRD STRUCTURAL SUPPORT
personalizedFeedback.description: Your primary aesthetic limitation is the *lack of horizontal bone growth* in the lower third. The narrow jaw and weak chin projection create a tapered look that lacks masculinity. To fix this, a *genioplasty* (chin advancement) or a *mandibular angle implant* would be required to increase the bigonial width and create a more defined, square jawline.

personalizedFeedback.title: ORBITAL COMPACTNESS
personalizedFeedback.description: You exhibit *high upper eyelid exposure*, which gives the eyes a tired or "droopy" appearance. This is usually a result of shallow orbital sockets and a lack of brow support. While some of this can be mitigated by *reducing overall facial fat* to sharpen the orbital rim, a permanent fix for the eyelid shape would require a *blepharoplasty* or similar corrective procedure to reduce the visible eyelid skin.

personalizedFeedback.title: MIDFACE HARMONY
personalizedFeedback.description: The *vertical elongation* of your midface disrupts the overall harmony of your face. This "stretched" look is a result of the ratio between your facial width and length. Since bone length cannot be reduced naturally, the goal should be to *increase the perceived width* of the face through the jaw and cheekbone development mentioned above, which will balance the verticality.

personalizedFeedback.title: LIP VOLUME AND DEFINITION
personalizedFeedback.description: Your lips are *structurally thin*, particularly the upper lip, which makes the lower third look underdeveloped. This contributes to the overall "weak" read of the lower face. *Lip fillers* or a surgical lip lift could increase the vertical height and projection, providing a more balanced transition between the nose and the chin.

personalizedFeedback.title: FACIAL DEFINITION
personalizedFeedback.description: There is a layer of *soft tissue* that obscures what little bone definition you have. By reaching a *lower body fat percentage* (roughly 10-12%), you can reduce the puffiness in the cheeks and under the chin. This will not fix the underlying bone structure, but it will make the existing jawline and cheekbones more visible, potentially raising your harmony score.

Your current skin quality is the most immediate limiting factor. You have *active acne* and congestion on your cheeks which obscures your bone structure and reduces your overall harmony.

personalizedFeedback.title: LIP VOLUME AND DEFINITION
personalizedFeedback.description:
Your lips, particularly the upper lip, are *thin and inconspicuous*. This creates a slight imbalance in the lower third of your face and reduces the "pretty" appeal of your features.
To fix this, you can look into *hyaluronic acid fillers* for the upper lip to create a more balanced volume and a more defined Cupid's bow.

personalizedFeedback.title: MIDFACE COMPRESSION
personalizedFeedback.description:
The *elongated midface* is a structural issue that makes your face appear longer than it is wide. This is caused by the vertical growth of the maxilla and the spacing of the features.
While bone length cannot be changed naturally, you can visually compensate by *increasing lower-third volume* through jawline development or by choosing hairstyles that add width to the sides of your head to balance the verticality.

personalizedFeedback.title: FACIAL DIMORPHISM AND WIDTH
personalizedFeedback.description:
Your *fWHR is relatively low*, meaning your face is narrow. This gives you a more youthful, softer look but lacks the "masculine" impact of a wider bizygomatic/bigonial ratio.
Focusing on *reducing overall body fat* to a lean percentage (10-12%) will help sharpen the existing jawline and cheekbones, making the narrowness look like "lean definition" rather than "weak structure."

personalizedFeedback.title: LOWER THIRD HARMONY
personalizedFeedback.description:
The combination of a slightly long philtrum and thin lips makes the lower third feel *stretched*.
Improving *tongue posture (mewing)* over a long period may provide marginal support to the maxilla, but for a significant change in the lower third's vertical height, orthodontic consultation regarding the *vertical dimension* of your bite would be the only definitive fix.
